beats.narration: Coins: one, three, four. Make six with the fewest.
Biggest first: four, one, one. {greedy.count} coins.
For this coin set, biggest-first isn't always best.

sources.claim: With coins 1, 3, 4: largest-first pays 6 as 4 + 1 + 1, while the minimum is 2 coins (3 + 3); dynamic programming and exhaustive enumeration agree
Largest-first is optimal for some coin systems (e.g. 1, 5, 10, 25) but not all
sources.ref: Kozen & Zaks (1994), Optimal bounds for the change-making problem, Theoretical Computer Science 123(2):377-388, https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-3975(94)90134-1; 1-500 checked in src/sims/puzzles.test.ts

post.caption:
Coins worth 1, 3 and 4. Make 6 with as few coins as possible.

Taking the biggest coin that fits (the greedy strategy) gives 4 + 1 + 1: three coins. But 3 + 3 does it in two.

This coin set is a counterexample, not a rule: for coins like 1, 5, 10, 25, biggest-first always finds the fewest. We checked 1, 3, 4 with a full search of every combination. Can you find another amount where greedy loses?
